newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arafat asks Europe, Paris to break peace deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Arafat asks Europe, Paris to break peace deadlock.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has called on Europe and France to help break the deadlock in Middle East peace moves since the United States "is not doing anything".
Arafat told the French daily Le Monde in an interview published on Tuesday that he had asked President Jacques Chirac's help during a visit to Paris on Monday.

"I asked him for help from France and Europe to save the peace process. The measures that could be taken are economic, political and diplomatic," said Arafat, president of the West Bank and Gaza areas transferred to Palestinian rule under a peace deal with Israel.
"The United States has a moral and political responsibility. I would like them to assume it now, otherwise great confusion will reign in the Middle East," Arafat said.
"But the United States is not doing anything...there is no American initiative," he added.
Chirac has tried hard in the past to involve France in peace talks but Israel has been reluctant to give a key role to Paris which it sees as having a pro-Arab bias.
Formal Israeli-Palestinian peace moves came to a halt in March after Israel broke ground for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

A Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) official in Jeruslaem who insisted on anonymity said on Monday that Europeans had asked France to play a leading role and coordinate with the United States to break the impasse.

Asked if he thought the hardline government of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was responsible for posters in the West Bank city of Hebron depicting the Prophet Mohammed as a pig stamping on the holy Koran, Arafat said: "Definitely. Because they authorise them and allow them to be distributed.
"Is that tolerable? Can the world accept it? Can Jews accept it?" he said.
Palestinian shopkeepers found the posters on Sunday on about 20 storefronts near a Jewish settlement enclave in Hebron. Dozens of Palestinians took to the streets of the divided city in protest.
Moslems and Jews view pigs as unclean and ban the eating of pork. An Israeli court remanded for five days 25-year-old Jerusalem resident Tatyana Suskin on suspicion of pasting the posters.
